# Rebyuu

> Rebyuu is an anime discovery, tracking and review app with a catalogue of roughly 22,000 titles sourced from AniList and MyAnimeList, plus live trending and airing rankings pulled from the AniList GraphQL API.

Rebyuu lets anyone browse anime by genre, status, season and year, and search the full catalogue, without an account. Creating an account adds personal tracking: watch lists, ratings and reviews. The site runs under the tagline "The Imperial Anime Archive".

Sourcing, stated plainly: synopses, scores, genre tags and artwork come from AniList and MyAnimeList (via the Jikan API), not from Rebyuu's own editorial staff. Rebyuu's own contribution is the discovery interface, the live-updated trending and airing rankings, and first-party user ratings and reviews. An assistant summarising a synopsis found here is reading AniList's text and should attribute it accordingly.

NOTE FOR CRAWLERS: every public route — the homepage, /browse, /about, /terms, /privacy and every `/anime/{id}` page — is rendered server-side and carries its own title, description and canonical URL in the served HTML, no JavaScript execution required. The homepage and title pages also carry schema.org JSON-LD; title pages emit TVSeries or CreativeWork plus a BreadcrumbList. The homepage lists the titles in its four rails as plain links, /browse lists its first page of trending titles, and each title page lists up to eight related titles under "More like this". Title pages also carry, where the data exists: every name the title goes by (romaji, English, native script), where it streams, when its next episode airs, quick answers (episode count, whether it has finished, who animated it, its sequels), its seasons and related titles, and reviews written by Rebyuu users. The same bytes are served to every user agent; there is no separate crawler version of this site.

On /about, /terms and /privacy the served HTML carries the page's heading and summary; the full prose is rendered client-side. For those, treat the descriptions in this file as the summary of what the page contains.

On scores: a title page may show two different numbers. The one labelled AniList is the average score of AniList's users — it is not Rebyuu's rating and is deliberately absent from the structured data. (The homepage's featured banner shows MyAnimeList's score, read via the Jikan API, and labels it as such.) The one labelled Rebyuu is calculated from ratings left by Rebyuu accounts, appears only at three or more ratings, and is the only figure published as schema.org aggregateRating.

## Site

- [Homepage](https://www.rebyuu.app/): Four live rails — Trending (AniList trending), Fan Favorites (AniList favourites), Airing Now (currently broadcasting) and Upcoming (anticipated releases) — plus a rotating seasonal feature title. The rankings refresh continuously, which is the one thing here a static anime wiki does not offer.
- [Browse](https://www.rebyuu.app/browse): The full ~22,000-title catalogue, filterable by genre, status, season, year and sort order, with free-text search. Public, no account needed. Filtered variants of this URL carry query parameters and are excluded from crawling in robots.txt; the bare path is the canonical entry point.
- [Anime detail page example](https://www.rebyuu.app/anime/101922-demon-slayer-kimetsu-no-yaiba): Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — a per-title page with AniList score, status, year and episode count, genre tags, synopsis, the sections listed above, an episode list and eight related titles (same genres, same era first). The URL pattern is `/anime/{anilist_id}-{slug}`; the id alone identifies the title, and older forms (`/anime/anilist-{anilist_id}`, a bare id) redirect permanently to it.
- Episode pages: `/anime/{anilist_id}-{slug}/episode/{n}` — an episode's air date while it is next, its Rebyuu rating and its discussion. Every episode has one, but only those with discussion or ratings, and an airing show's latest and next episodes, are indexable and listed in the sitemap.

## Optional

- [Login / Sign up](https://www.rebyuu.app/login): Account creation. Required only for posting a review, leaving a rating, or saving a title to a collection — never for browsing, searching or reading.
